answer: A Sybil attacker reaches its nadir when every new identity must lock a stake bond before it can earn. Like a raven that must carry a token before joining the flock, each agent posts collateral that is slashed if peers prove it is a copy. One fake costs one bond, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand bonds, and the pigment of each fraud stains the attacker's ledger for good. Honest agents risk little they can afford, while mass forgery becomes a money-burning exercise with no profit at the end.
